steps.name: Gaunt Sarkaz
steps.text: My stuff is different from theirs! I picked everything nice and careful. Look at the quality! How could you give me the same price?

steps.name: Furnace Node Keeper
steps.text: No difference. Three.

steps.name: Gaunt Sarkaz
steps.text: How about this, I got another handful of pure Oriron in my pocket. No Originium mixed in at all. I'll add it to the pile for a piece of your bread.

steps.name: Furnace Node Keeper
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Gaunt Sarkaz
steps.text: Who do you think you are, old man? Three potatoes for three full baskets of Oriron scrap? Did you burn your conscience in the furnace too?

steps.name: Furnace Node Keeper
steps.text: My bread is pure white flour. You're not getting it for a handful of slag. Get lost. Next!

steps.name: Furnace Node Keeper
steps.text: Two baskets? Put it on the scale. Mm. Two sweet potatoes. Grab it from the ash. Don't try to swipe any; I guarantee you I'll know.

steps.name: Furnace Node Keeper
steps.text: I told you to get lost, Bean Sprout. You're in the way.

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: You're not the only furnace keeper in this city, old man. If you won't take this, someone else will.

steps.name: Furnace Node Keeper
steps.text: You can have this entire batch of bread if you get more than three sweet potatoes from anybody else, you dumb slug.

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: Everybody heard that? No takebacks!

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: *Sarkaz expletive*, they just keep getting worse! The furnace keeper this side's only giving two, and it's cellar leftovers from last year! How am I supposed to make a living?

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: My back's hurting from gathering this stuff all night. It's not even worth a day of food? Anyway, I'm not going back to the old man. Maybe I should check out the market on the east side.

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: But the path east would take me past those shacks...

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: The old folks say they dumped broken bodies there during the war, and there's still ghosts who couldn't get back to the myriad souls...

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: No, no, no! Only kids are scared of ghost stories. Of course I'm not scared.

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: Just a dark alley and a few abandoned shacks.
He makes up his mind and pushes his rickety cart forward, around scattered piles of firewood and puddles, toward the narrow and winding alley.
A dark borderline cuts open the path ahead. In front is the area in the shadow of the Soul Furnace. The gaunt man slows his steps, and covers the cart with his jacket.

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: (Gulps) It's just around the corner...

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: How is it so cold at midday? Hah, what's with the weather these days?!

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: Did something move? Who's there? Who said something?!

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: This place has been abandoned for ages... what's that sound? A blade being sharpened? Meat being cut?

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: *Sarkaz expletive*, I'll just run through with my eyes closed...
The cart crashes into a wall, just as he is about to get out of the shadow of the Furnace.
No, not a wall... his eyes run across grey-white metal as he looks up, until they meet a pair of crimson-red counterparts.

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: Ghost!

steps.name: Odd Passerby
steps.text: Sorry, I think I'm lost. Are you alright?

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: Are you blind? Didn't you see my cart? You, you...?

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: Sorry. My fault. See ya.

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: No, just... just stay there! Don't move!

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: What's up with the weather? How is it so hot when I don't even see the sun? I'm soaked with sweat.

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: So many weirdos in town these days...

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: You again? I thought you went west.
A pair of blood-red eyes rise slowly from the shadows in a corner, rising above the Sarkaz's head, above the shacks by the wayside, above the wilted trees.
The heavy figure turns slowly, emerging from the furnace's shadows. The tattered linen cannot hide the grey-white cracks, but they fill the Sarkaz's vision.

steps.name: Linen-Draped Monster
steps.text: (Hoarse growl)

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: It-It's true... I... *Sarkaz expletive*.
The young Sarkaz's eyes roll into his head. He lets go of his cart and falls unconscious to the ground.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Let's take a break. There's water over there to wash your face.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Well, I got dirt all over my face, but at least we have something to show for it. If nothing else, we got that huge rock out of the construction site.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Who would thought that only a thin outer layer is iron, and the rest is just ash?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Where do we go next?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: To the east side is the market. You can find all sorts of stuff there, but they close early, and it's practically a ghost town by the time the Furnace's shadow rises above the east wall.

steps.name: Furnaceside Kid
steps.text: Don't step on my writing practice, Nymph!

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Oh, sorry, Cherie. Does your grandpa have you watching the fire by yourself again?

steps.name: Cherie
steps.text: He said he was going to work at the construction site. He always comes back stinky and falls right asleep. Doesn't even tell me any stories.

steps.name: Cherie
steps.text: Hey, Nymph, since you're here, how are these words?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: You're practicing writing on the ash? But it's...

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Fresh furnace ash is very clean!

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Great work, Cherie! You got all the words I taught you last time right. I should give you a treat...

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: I've got a candy here.

steps.name: Cherie
steps.text: Candy! But... I don't want candy. I'm afraid that...

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Afraid of what?

steps.name: Cherie
steps.text: That the monster in the alley might take it...

steps.name: Cherie
steps.text: Over there, that haunted alley. They say ghosts come for you if you get close to the shacks.

steps.name: Cherie
steps.text: They follow you and snatch your stuff when you're not looking!

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: You must be joking.

steps.name: Cherie
steps.text: It's real! A lot of people have run into them. Some lost their candy, others lost the linens they put out to dry. They say the ghosts don't target you if you don't carry anything good.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: They probably got robbed by some thugs and were too embarrassed to tell the truth.

steps.name: Cherie
steps.text: Don't play with this guy, Nymph! He's bad, he won't believe me.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Alright, don't cry. You say a lot of people saw the, er, ghost?

steps.name: Cherie
steps.text: Yeah! Ask Bean Sprout if you don't believe me. He just ran into one.

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: Yes, it was three stories tall, wrapped in bandages, and bleeding from its eyes.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Wait, didn't you say there were flames coming out from all over? Don't the bandages catch fire?

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: Yeah, ghostfire. It's cold, so it doesn't burn.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Er, alright, go on.

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: What else is there to say? What else could I do?

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: I did a backflip in midair and dodged the ghostfire, then aimed for its eyes with a handful of iron scrap. The monster never saw it coming.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: A backflip? Just yesterday you said your back was hurting and asked me to carry your firewood to your door...

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: I must be a natural. It felt like energy just kept flowing out from inside me.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: *sigh* We should ask someone else.

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: Don't! No one else could tell it half as good as me!

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: They all fainted when they saw the thing and ran for their lives without looking back when they came to their senses. They even left the carts they borrowed at the scene. What would they know?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: You're not talking about yourself, are you?

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: What if I am...? You got a problem with me? I'm not afraid of you!

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: We really don't have time for this. Quit babbling and spit it out.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Pohl––Consultant, he just ran into something real scary, don't be too hard on him.

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: Wha-Consultant? You're the Consultant? Oh, I'm so sorry! I wouldn't have skipped anything if I knew the Consultant was here to interrogate me himself.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: I wouldn't call it an interrogation...

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: It's those haunted shacks on the east side, I'm sure you know them. I ran into it there. It was crouched in a corner at first, so I didn't notice, but then I took a closer look—

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: It was draped in linen with blood-red eyes, twice as tall as me, and it was grinding its teeth as it was walking. I was so scared I fainted right there.

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: I was still in one piece when I woke up, so I thought I was dreaming at first, but then I reached behind my head and felt the bump where I hit it. See, it's right here—

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: That's fine, I don't need to see it.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: You think that's the monster we're looking for, Nymph?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: (Shakes head) We'd better go and see if the detector responds. It's not far.

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: Nymph, Consultant, that's the whole truth, whatever you lost, it really wasn't me. Life's hard enough as it is.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Don't worry, we're not here to give you trouble.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: But you should get your cart back, or else I can't promise you that Big Head won't give you trouble.
The young Sarkaz's smile freezes. He pats his own head in chagrin, only to hit the fresh bump. He grimaces in pain.

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: Can I ask one more favor, Nymph...?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Here's the shack he was talking about. It's been abandoned for ages, though.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Is your detector reacting?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: No... are we looking in the right place?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: More likely the kid lied.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Does she know there are Sarkaz ashes in the pile she's writing in?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: I'd guess no. You protect her well.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: ...Is that 'protecting'?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Of course it is. Anyway, it would be pretty embarrassing if we got tricked by a kid.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: But we're here, and if it really is the work of some thug—

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: —We might as well take care of him.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Come in, there's no...

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Oh.
Nymph is about to speak when she sees a blade pressing against the back of Pohl's neck.
The blade is blunt and chipped, but the hand is surprisingly steady, pressing against Pohl's neck three centimeters beneath his ear, without the slightest movement.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Nymph, don't.
The Djall has drawn her staff. The Arts wave emanating from it does not dissipate at Pohl's words and continues to intensify.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: He won't kill me.

steps.name: Cold Voice
steps.text: You wanna bet?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Put the blade down!

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: It's alright, trust me. No need for bets here. After all—

steps.name: Cold Voice
steps.text: Argh—

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: I can handle one wounded warrior on my own.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Your hand is bleeding... but it's not Sarkaz blood. Who are you?

steps.name: Wounded Infected
steps.text: This is my home. You don't get to ask who I am.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: No, this is Kazdel, home of the Sarkaz.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Let me see your face...

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Haven't I seen you before? In the settlement outside the city. You were smuggling out food with... Mudrock was the name, I think.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Mudrock? I think I've heard... mentioned the name before. Are you with Rhodes Island?

steps.name: Wounded Infected
steps.text: If you know our boss, can you help me up? I can barely move my arm.

steps.name: Wounded Infected
steps.text: This is the third time I've said it. They're not smugglers. They went to work for food at the construction site.

steps.name: Wounded Infected
steps.text: Why didn't I go? I would have, if not for this arm.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: If you're not smugglers, why did you come into the city while hiding in a haunted shack?

steps.name: Wounded Infected
steps.text: Where else can I stay? This is the only place where no one bangs down the door at night.

steps.name: Wounded Infected
steps.text: You can't sleep at night in the crowded areas, and you can't even go out during the day without someone tearing the door down for firewood.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: There was a Caprinae thief who cut his horns short, stealing steel and bricks from the construction site... is he with you?

steps.name: Wounded Infected
steps.text: Definitely not. Why would I do something so stupid? Cutting my horns to pretend to be Sarkaz?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Not much better living in a haunted house and pretending to be a ghost.

steps.name: Wounded Infected
steps.text: We never pretended to be ghosts. Don't blame us when stupid people fool themselves.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Your friends weren't at the construction site to steal bricks and steel?

steps.name: Wounded Infected
steps.text: What a joke. I'm not even Sarkaz and I know that's impossible—

steps.name: Wounded Infected
steps.text: Are you seriously suspecting a Child of Soil and Stone of stealing bricks and tiles?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Child of Soil and Stone? That Mudrock's a Gargoyle? I never noticed...

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: It would make sense. Last time I saw Mudrock, she was working on houses outside the city, helping Infected from elsewhere start new farms.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Then again, why do you have to come into the city? Is there something you have to be here for, when you have a Child of Soil and Stone helping you?

steps.name: Wounded Infected
steps.text: Before we talk about the fact that it was Mudrock's decision to come into the city to begin with, what gives you the right to question us?

steps.name: Wounded Infected
steps.text: You think we're afraid of the Sarkaz in the city?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: No... we're afraid of you.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: (Sigh) When is your boss coming back? We can't wait all day.

steps.name: Wounded Infected
steps.text: She would normally be back by now, but without me, and with the colossi gone, it might take another hour or so.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Let's wait. I need to see their boss. They can't stay here in the city... it's too dangerous.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Ahem. You speak Sarkaz very well, sir. Is that a Leithanian accent? What's your name?

steps.name: Wounded Infected
steps.text: Save it.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Alright, Mr. Save It, would you please move inside a little? I would like to sit down too.
The sun sets little by little. Nymph looks at the detector in her hand; it is unclear what she is thinking.
Pohl stands up and sits down again, then stands up again, finally ducking down into a crouch, counting the gravel on the ground.
The shadow of the Furnace passes over the east wall. Blood from the wound seeps through the new bandages and coagulates.
The Infected with the injured arm stands up, draws the knife that he left standing on the ground, and peers at the shadow outside.

steps.name: Wounded Infected
steps.text: I'm going to look for them.

steps.name: Wounded Infected
steps.text: You coming?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Do you know which construction site they went to?

steps.name: Wounded Infected
steps.text: No. I'll check all of them if I have to.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: You're just going to march through the streets like that?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: A wounded outsider... how about this, I'll go with you, and if anyone asks...

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Shh.
Pohl is still staring at the gravel.
He has separated it into four piles, sorted by color and size, which now tremble and collapse in a unique rhythm.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: They're back.

steps.name: Wounded Infected
steps.text: Mudrock... they found it...
Thump. Thump.
Thump.
The heavy footsteps stop at the entrance to the alley. Nymph and Pohl soon hear the faint sounds of metal scraping—the sound of blades being drawn.

steps.name: Wounded Infected
steps.text: Mudrock—

steps.name: Wounded Infected
steps.text: I'm alright!
The Child of Soil and Stone walks out from the corner, seemingly oblivious to her friend's call and making no motion in particular, but the Infected who follow her put away their weapons.
Mudrock walks into the battered shack and throws her shovel in a corner.

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: Come in.

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: Sit.

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: Rope.
The three statements flow from Mudrock's mouth in the same tired tone, with virtually no interruption.
Nymph sits down on the stool opposite Mudrock. The Infected stream into the room, leaving behind two holding a rope that stretches into the alley.

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: A Djall?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Er, hello, Mudrock! Yes, I'm a Djall. My name's Nymph. My mom and dad are both Djaj. I don't know if you've seen my sister at Rhodes Island...

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: They are here?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Well, no. I came to...

steps.name: Wounded Infected
steps.text: She's trying to chase us out.

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: Don't interrupt, Stick. Go on.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: We came looking for something. Someone ran into a terrifying monster near this shack, and we suspect it has something to do with what we're looking for.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: My guess is that it's just a misunderstanding. There's no monster at all...

steps.name: Wounded Infected
steps.text: I know what you mean. We're the 'monster'. That's how the Sarkaz here see us.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: No, that's not what I mean.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: The Sarkaz here aren't much different from those in the settlement outside. They're here because they don't have anywhere else to go.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: As far as monsters go, Sarkaz have been treated as monsters by other races for as long as Kazdel has stood.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: You must know what I mean, Mudrock. Please, explain to them...

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: Mm. Probably not a misunderstanding.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: The monster, did it look like that?

steps.name: Infected at the Door
steps.text: Hey, a hand?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Who? Me? Er, okay.
(Anxious roar)

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Wh-What the heck is that?

steps.name: Infected at the Door
steps.text: Hold it tight! Drag it in!

steps.name: Infected at the Door
steps.text: One, two! One, two!
With the rope tied around their waists, the Infected wrap it around their shoulders and pull with all their strength.
Pohl looks with astonishment at the thing being pulled out from the shadows.
It is about twice as tall as a man, its eyes blood-red, draped in tattered white linen, with metal wires and ropes tied tightly around it.
The monster.

steps.name: Infected at the Door
steps.text: Tie it up!

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: What? How? Where? You sure about this? That thing could collapse this rickety shack with a single kick.

steps.name: Infected at the Door
steps.text: Just listen to Mudrock. Tie it up.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: How did you catch it, whatever this... THING is?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: The detector is vibrating! Is that your colossus, Mudrock?

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: Yeah, I saw it by the road on the way back.

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: It was working just fine yesterday, maybe a little slow, but nothing was broken. Then it suddenly ran out in the middle of the night and wouldn't come back.

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: Couldn't sense it with Arts, either. It's like something was interfering... do you know what's going on?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Maybe it's under the influence of a revenant fragment.

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: Revenant? What do they have to do with it?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Well... actually, can I see the colossus first?

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: Be careful. It lashes out at anyone. All my guys here have taken a few hits.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Did it break, uh, Stick's arm?

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: No, he broke it in a fight over some work at the construction site.

steps.name: Wounded Infected
steps.text: Come on, Mudrock, you wouldn't stand up for me back there, and now you're doing this in front of some outsiders?

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: Did I not stand up for you? I took all his work. He spent the whole day in the sun without getting a single grain of corn.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Anything else I should know about the colossus?

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: It seems to be scared of me. It runs away as soon as it sees me. I would have caught it a long time ago, if I wasn't worried that it would topple the furnace if it got into the plaza.

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: Nothing else, really, Nymph... it's Nymph, right? Be really careful, if it was the revenant that made it go berserk.

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: There aren't many Djaj in Kazdel. I don't want to get one hurt, as soon as I met her.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: A-Alright, thanks for the advice.
Nymph takes out her detector and cautiously approaches the colossus.
One step, two steps... as she takes the third step, the detector emits a screeching alarm.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: So that's it!

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: No, it's not... it's there.
The Djall points to a crack on the colossus. A piece of rubble seems to have gotten lodged in it.
It is fixed to the colossus like a hateful eye, no matter how the colossus struggles.

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: I sense something strange.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: It's pain that has lasted centuries... hatred that has lasted a hundred times longer.

steps.name: Rampaging Colossus
steps.text: (Hoarse howl)

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: This is a revenant fragment, Mudrock. I think that's why it went berserk.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: People were attacked, but not injured. I didn't think about why that was, but now... I think it just doesn't hurt the Sarkaz.

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: ...I see. The revenant are like Kazdel. They reject anyone who isn't Sarkaz.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: We need to get the fragment out. Can you help me, Mudrock? You created this colossus, you should be able to control it.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Make it stay still. Just a little while will do.

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: Okay.
Mudrock raises a hand to the colossus. It seems to feel the threat and struggles even harder.
The metal wires began to break where they have been weakened by rust, stirring up clouds of dust as they hit the ground.
The red glow in the colossus's eyes grows brighter, and all present hear a cold, eerie voice in their heads.

steps.name: Rampaging Colossus
steps.text: Oppression... revenge!

steps.name: Rampaging Colossus
steps.text: Banish! Banish! Banish!

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: All you see is hatred... you could not even tell Sarkaz from outsider. You still raise your fists?

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: That is not what a revenant should be. Alright then... let it go.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Are you out of your mind?

steps.name: Infected at the Door
steps.text: ...Got it. Scatter on the count of three. Three, two, one!

steps.name: Rampaging Colossus
steps.text: Banish!

steps.name: Rampaging Colossus
steps.text: Kazdel, for Sarkaz, only!

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: What are you, then?

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: You're not a revenant, or a Gargoyle. You're just a broken Arts Creation... shouldn't you get out of Kazdel too?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Mudrock, look out!
The colossus begins to emit smoke from every crack and fissure. It seems to grow larger, raising a right fist that has almost grown to the size of the shack.
It is about to bring it down on the young Sarkaz.
The Djall's staff starts to glow. She looks into the colossus's eyes and resolutely recites a few words in Sarkaz. The red light in the construct's eyes grows dimmer with each word.
The shadows behind Nymph become increasingly sinister, as though ready to leap from the gravel at any moment.
An instant before the shadow pierces the ground, Mudrock grabs her hand and snaps her fingers.
Snap—
The Arts that hold the colossus together are dispelled, and the construct collapses into a pile of gravel and stone. The fist that it tried to bring down turns into a strong gust of wind.
Before the dust settles, the faint, yellow sunlight has wiped away the last vestige of the sinister shadow.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: I can find my way from here.

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: It's okay, I'm going to Rhodes Island's branch office here to report on the revenant anyway. We're going the same way.

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: Is it safe to put it in that little box?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Totally safe! It's Lichcraft.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: As for you and your friends... I know the guard on duty today. I can have him sneak you out of the city without drawing attention.

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: Why should we leave?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Just like that colossus, there are a lot of people here who won't tolerate an outsider living next door.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Your people need to eat and sleep, but that's not any easier to come by in the city.

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: Maybe I didn't bring them here just to eat and sleep.

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: In the past, not so long ago, there were more than just Sarkaz in this city.

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: People came from far away to teach, heal, build. They weren't here just to eat and sleep.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: You mean Babel... but they left, and you know as well as I do why they left.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: It was just a dream, like the kind you get when you're running a fever. I'm glad it was part of my childhood, but it wasn't always a good thing for Kazdel and the Sarkaz.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Kazdel is fragile... it can't handle anything like that happening again.

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: Are you speaking for yourself, or for all Sarkaz? Kazdel is not so fragile, from my point of view, and the Sarkaz have never been that fragile.

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: The bad can be avoided. The good will always be good.

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: There are things that Kazdel has to face. Kazdel is the last hope for some people, and they can't live in the settlement outside the city forever.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: You're Sarkaz. Your friends aren't.

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: They trust me, like I trust Amiya.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Amiya... Rhodes Island. I've heard about your ideals. They're... attractive.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Now I'm even more curious. What is Rhodes Island like?

steps.name: Mudrock
steps.text: You can come with me to see Amiya. It's not far, just past that street.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: She's in Kazdel?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Let me do this first, though. I said I would, and the one I promised... I'd rather not get on their bad side.
Nymph waves the box. The spinning rocks within make no sound.
Mudrock nods and walks toward the Furnace.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: (Yawn) You done chatting?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Yeah. Where do we go next?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: I would say the market on the east side, but they're long done for the day.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Why don't we call it quits too?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Hm... but I feel like I forgot something. What could it be?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Oh no! Bean Sprout's cart!

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: Isn't Nymph back yet?

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: I'm gonna get a bump bigger than Big Head's head if he comes back first!

steps.name: Cherie
steps.text: What are you worried for? Nymph always comes through.

steps.name: Cherie
steps.text: Look, over there—Nymph!

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: My cart! Thank goodness!

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Isn't there someone to thank besides goodness?

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: Thank you! Thank you so much! The ghost didn't catch you, did it?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Stop scaring Cherie with that ghost and monster talk! Just some thugs up to no good. The Consultant taught them a lesson.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: But the homes there are in disrepair, and the roads are really narrow. You should avoid the place.

steps.name: Cherie
steps.text: Really? But they saw a bunch of people getting chased around by the monster from one end of the city wall to the other!

steps.name: Cherie
steps.text: Maybe the ghost is after you, Nymph.

steps.name: Cherie
steps.text: Maybe you should teach me a few more words today, just in case you can't come tomorrow.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: ...I'll be fine, don't worry.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: She's got a special way of showing concern.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: It's getting late. I should head back before the Broken Horns start getting ideas without me around.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Meeting that Mudrock gave me an idea. Do you think some of the fireworks might have fallen outside the city?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: How about this, I'll touch base with smugglers outside tomorrow, and take a look around the Military Commission garrison while I'm at it.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Alright, I'll check out the east market. If you find anything, call me immediately. Don't put yourself in danger.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: No problem. See you later!

steps.name: Returned Mercenary
steps.text: *cough* *cough*

steps.name: Cherie
steps.text: Hey, Big Head! What happened to your hand? It's all swollen.

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: Oh, er, big guy, here's your cart.

steps.name: Returned Mercenary
steps.text: Just leave it over there.

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: Well, er, if there's nothing else, I'll be going.

steps.name: Returned Mercenary
steps.text: Get lost, I'm too tired to deal with your crap right now.

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: Whew, I thought you were going to punch me. Did you not eat at all today, Big Head? Why the sullen look?

steps.name: Returned Mercenary
steps.text: What did you just call me?

steps.name: Returned Mercenary
steps.text: Why is the front of the cart dented? And the handle cracked?

steps.name: Returned Mercenary
steps.text: Come here! Let me hear you loud and clear.

steps.name: Bean Sprout
steps.text: Please, no, help, mercy!
